instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Hidden Power
cards.instruction: Act publicly modest while making choices as though you control the outcome.

cards.title: One Last Thing
cards.instruction: Keep someone present by discovering one more small task, question, or favor whenever departure seems near.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only closing up. Before you go, could you check the window latch? I'll leave that one till you've tried it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's shut. Goodbye.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll draw the curtain first, then. Why's it moving if the window's shut? Could you have a look?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The fan's on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll have the fan off before we finish. Could you show me which switch? I'll leave the others alone till you've pointed it out.

beats.text: I'm only tidying up after you. One last cup to dry before your taxi arrives; I'll put everything else away.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Done. My taxi's here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll keep that cup on the top shelf. Could you reach it for me? I'll fetch your coat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put him on speaker for a moment. I'll thank him before we open the door. Could you tell me his name first?

cards.title: You Could at Least…
cards.instruction: Make the inconvenience visible enough that an apology becomes the easiest way forward.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only setting the table. I've put my wet sock beside your plate, so you can see what your puddle did.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's only water.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll leave it there while I bring the food in. I've moved your glass so the sock has room.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you move the sock instead?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Say you're sorry and I'll clear it away. I'd rather serve dinner than find somewhere to hang the other wet one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only clearing the table. I'll leave this timetable out: three buses I missed waiting for you to bring my keys back.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was only twenty minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Three circles. I'll put the takeaway receipt beside it, from when my dinner was still hot.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll buy another dinner. Can we put the papers away?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep your money. Say you're sorry and I'll clear the lot; otherwise I'll need this end of the table to show you where the evening went.

cards.title: Just Say Yes
cards.instruction: Get a quick approval before anyone has time to examine the practical consequences.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only handling the booking. Quick yes to the garden party before the date expires? I'll deal with the details.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How many guests?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll count the chairs after I've secured the date. Just give me the yes now.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: And the cost?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll bring the quote over while you say yes. I'll confirm first, then you can read it without the booking disappearing underneath us.

cards.title: Your Turn
cards.instruction: Get someone to accept responsibility for a task you believe should never have been yours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only putting the cleaning things away. Your name's beside bathroom duty, so I'll leave the mop with you. It was never my turn.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're better at it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You'll get the practice tonight. I'll set the bucket by the bathroom and leave the clear floor for you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you show me first?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. Take the mop and tell me you're doing the bathroom; I'll point out where to start while you get the water.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I only covered your bins while you were away. I'll change the group contact back to you tonight; I didn't take the job on permanently.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The neighbours send all the reminders to you now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll introduce you as their permanent bin contact and put your number at the top. Thursday's yours.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will you stay in the group until I know what I'm doing?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Until you send 'I'll handle Thursday'. I'll wait for that message, then leave the group while they welcome you. You can answer their questions.

cards.title: What Was the Plan?
cards.instruction: Find out what was promised, scheduled, or changed without revealing that you lost track.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only typing the invitations. I'll check the details before anything goes out. What time did we settle on for Mum's dinner?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Seven, in the private room. You booked it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. I'll keep the wording consistent with yours. How have you written the restaurant name?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I haven't written anything. You're doing the invitations.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The confirmation's on my screen. Read it aloud while I type, starting with the name; I'll use that as our master copy to avoid mistakes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only checking the weather. I'll choose what goes in tomorrow's walking reminder: are we taking the ridge or the river?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The ridge. We changed because the river path flooded.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll put the flood warning first. Where are we meeting? I'll decide which directions people need.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've asked me twice. Have you forgotten your own itinerary?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm checking it works without my help. Give me the briefing you'd give a newcomer, starting with where I report. I'll take the notes for everyone.
